blanks.sentence: Screen time refers to the amount of time spent using digital _____ such as phones, tablets and laptops. (1)
Australia has restricted social media access for _____.
The expert does not argue for removing technology, but for being more _____ in how adults use it with children. (3)
Product design should put _____ rather than technology itself at the centre. (4)
Technology should support children’s learning and _____. (5)
Saying that “the bar needs to be higher” means adults should raise their _____ about children’s technology use. (6)
Many parents want _____ things they can do at home.
Parents may benefit from making _____ rather than dramatic changes. (8)
One suggested strategy is reducing the device’s _____ in the room. (9)
Leaving the screen visible may fail to set the child up for _____. (10)

multipleChoice.question: What is meant by “screen time” in the discussion?
options: Time spent watching television only
Time spent using digital devices
Time spent studying online lessons
Time spent checking work messages

multipleChoice.question: Why is children’s device use presented as a public concern?
options: Children are unable to use laptops safely
Parents want schools to ban all technology
Australia has stopped children using all devices
Children may be spending too much time on devices

multipleChoice.question: How does Emily Goodacre frame the solution to children’s technology use?
options: Use technology more deliberately with children
Remove technology from children’s lives completely
Let children decide their own limits
Focus mainly on parents’ phone habits

multipleChoice.question: What does the explanation of “intentional” add to Emily’s view?
options: Technology should be used only for education
Children should avoid devices when possible
Adults should act with a clear purpose
Product designers should ignore children’s age

multipleChoice.question: What attitude is implied by saying “the bar needs to be higher”?
options: Current expectations may be too low
Children should meet fewer requirements
Technology companies have solved the problem
Parents should stop setting expectations

multipleChoice.question: What positive role might technology have, according to the summary of Emily’s view?
options: It can replace adult guidance
It can remove the need for limits
It can make children develop faster than normal
It can support children’s learning and development

multipleChoice.question: What does Becky Kennedy say many parents are looking for?
options: Scientific proof that screens are always harmful
Strict rules that apply to every family
Realistic actions they can take at home
A way to remove every device immediately

multipleChoice.question: What kind of change is introduced before Becky’s example?
options: A small adjustment in the home environment
A complete ban on screens at home
A formal punishment for device use
A new educational app for children

multipleChoice.question: Why might moving a visible screen help a child?
options: It teaches the child to use technology faster
It reduces the temptation created by seeing it
It proves the child dislikes screens
It makes the child responsible for adult choices

multipleChoice.question: What does the phrase “set them up for success” mean in this context?
options: Reward children after they use a screen
Let children learn by failing repeatedly
Make screen use more entertaining
Create conditions that help children succeed
